title: Latency-Fidelity Governor and Experimentation Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes the Latency-Fidelity Governor (LFG): an operational component that mediates runtime scheduling decisions to balance client-facing latency SLOs against model output fidelity and cost. It bundles architecture notes, scheduler integration patterns, profiling/benchmark procedures, rollout & release guidance, and an incident runbook.

Audience
--------
- Runtime owners and engineers implementing scheduling policies
- Oncall SREs responding to latency/fidelity incidents
- Applied ML engineers running fidelity regressions during quantization or model swaps

Goals
-----
1. Define a repeatable, observable control loop that enforces latency SLOs while minimizing fidelity regressions.
2. Provide concrete experimentation and rollout steps so teams can validate LFG changes in staging and production-like environments.
3. Standardize telemetry and profiling artifacts used in decisions and post-incident analysis.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
- Scope: scheduling policy surface (admission, preemption, kernel hints), governor controller, observability signals, benchmark harness, and incident playbook.
- Non-goals: model training, user-facing prompt engineering, or billing systems.

Design overview
---------------
High level: LFG is a control plane component that consumes real-time telemetry (latency quantiles, kernel queue lengths, token-throughput, KV cache hit rates, and quality metrics from evaluation hooks) and outputs: per-route admission thresholds, priority weights, and model-variant fallback directives.

Key concepts
------------
- Latency target (SLO): per-route 95p service time target (example: 95p <= 120 ms for short-completion routes).
- Fidelity budget: allowable delta in downstream eval metrics (e.g., Rouge-L, BLEU, hallucination P@K) vs baseline after model or quantization changes.
- Degradation modes: reduced beam size, fallback to larger model variant that runs on different kernel, or lower token-sampling temperature.
- Cost knob: quantization level and batching (higher batching reduces cost but increases tail latency).

Component interactions (text diagram)
-----------------------------------
1) Ingress router -> 2) Admission controller -> 3) LFG controller (observability inputs) -> 4) Kernel scheduler / slot allocator -> 5) Serving runtime (kernels + KV cache) -> 6) Eval hook (async quality probe) -> back to 3).

Controller behavior and ruleset (condensed)
-------------------------------------------
- Every 30s sliding window evaluate: 95p latency, avg queue length, KV hit rate, and sample eval success rate.
- If 95p > SLO by 15% and queue length high: lower admission rate for low-priority routes by 25% and escalate heavy requests to Dedicated pool (if configured).
- If async eval shows fidelity delta > budget and cost per token < configured cap: reduce batching aggressiveness and prefer higher-precision quantization profile for affected model route during peak windows.
- Always maintain a safety floor: preserve at least 5% capacity for high-priority low-latency routes.

Kernel scheduler integration
---------------------------
- Policy tokens: LFG emits kernel-hints as metadata on requests: {priority: P0|P1|P2, kernel_hint: fast_fwd|stable_prec, admission_deadline_ms: X}.
- Scheduler consumes these hints to decide slot assignment, preemption windows, and co-location affinity.
- When kernel switching is required (e.g., switch from quantized kernel to fp16 kernel for fidelity), controller triggers a gradual ramp using the runtime's canary matrix (see "Rollout checklist").

Telemetry and observability contract
-----------------------------------
Required signals (sample names):
- runtime.latency_ms.{route}.{quantile} (p50,p90,p95,p99)
- runtime.queue_length.{pool} (gauge)
- runtime.kv_hit_rate.{model} (ratio)
- runtime.kernel_dispatch_latency.{kernel_variant} (histogram)
- runtime.quality_probe.{route}.{metric} (value)
- runtime.cost_per_token.{route} (gauge)

When to run profiling and benchmarks
-----------------------------------
- Pre-merge: any code that touches admission, scheduling, or kernel selection must include unit tests and a microbenchmark showing performance delta.
- Pre-production canary: run the benchmark suite with the target synthetic load and the fidelity probe corpus.
- Rolling upgrade: for kernel or quantization changes run a 72-hour shadow-run against a 10% traffic mirror and collect fidelity and latency traces.

Profiling playbook (short)
-------------------------
1. Baseline capture: collect 1 hour of trace from production for the target route under normal load (traces must include kernel ids and KV cache annotations).
2. Micro-run: replay baseline with single-tenant microbench harness to reproduce tail artifacts. Command: 
   runtimectl profile --route /v1/generate --sample-hour 2026-07-09T14:00Z --out /tmp/trace.pb
3. Kernel-sensitivity sweep: iterate kernel variants with sequence-length buckets [8, 32, 128] and collect dispatch and execution times.
4. Fidelity probe: run evaluation harness with the same prompts used for quality gates. Command: 
   runtimectl eval --corpus corpora/latency-fidelity-corpus.jsonl --model v2.1-quantized --metrics rouge-l,bertscore --out /tmp/eval.json
5. Report: produce a combined PDF with latency quantiles, kernel breakdown, and fidelity deltas. Use the runtime-report tool.

Benchmark suite guidance
------------------------
- Run the system-wide benchmark harness (shell snippet):
  export BENCH_PROFILE=latency_fidelity_experiment
  benchctl run --config benchmarks/profiles/latency-fidelity.yml --duration 30m --collect-traces
- Benchmark profile should include: mixed route weights, client-side pacing, and session-affinity churn. Use three load shapes: steady, spike (x3 for 90s), and decay.
- Acceptance criteria: 95p latency within target and fidelity delta <= configured budget over 30m. If violated, abort rollout.

Runbook: incident response for sustained 95p regression
-----------------------------------------------------
- Trigger: alert runtime.latency_ms.{route}.p95 > SLO * 1.15 for 5m.
- Primary oncall steps (0–5m):
  1) Acknowledge and tag incident in PagerDuty with "LFG: latency regression".
  2) Check synthetic shadow-run status and recent admission changes.
  3) If admission throttles were applied in last 5 minutes, rollback last policy change.
- Triage (5–30m):
  1) Pull runtime.trace for top 10 slow requests; look for: kernel_dispatch_latency spikes, KV miss bursts, or increased preemption events.
  2) If KV miss rate > 10pp from baseline: trigger kvcache-warmup pipeline (see runbook kvcache-warmup).
  3) If kernel_dispatch_latency for a kernel variant is elevated by >25%: move traffic to an alternate kernel with the governor directive: LFG:set kernel_hint=stable_prec for route X.
- Mitigation (30–120m):
  1) Reduce batching target by 20% for affected pool.
  2) If capacity saturation is root cause, request Dedicated pool burst (for customers with Dedicated) or swap to a lower-cost model variant that preserves latency.
  3) Monitor fidelity probes continuously; if fidelity regressions exceed budget during mitigation, revert to baseline model.

Rollout checklist (for a new LFG policy or kernel variant)
--------------------------------------------------------
1. Unit tests and microbench coverage added (PR required).
2. Run local benchmark profile with synthetic load (pass).
3. Stage canary: 1% production traffic shadow + 0.5% live traffic, 24h collection.
4. Shadow run fidelity delta must be <= budget and 95p latency <= SLO + 5%.
5. Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 30–60m observation windows and automated rollback on policy triggers.
6. Release note snippet example: 
   - "LFG v1.3: Adds per-route dynamic batching and stable_prec kernel preference. Default fidelity budget: 0.5% BLEU delta. Auto-rollback on p95>120ms*1.15"

Known issues and mitigations (picked examples)
--------------------------------------------
- Intermittent KV-cache ripple: After large model swaps, initial KV misses cause higher tail latency. Mitigation: kvcache prewarm and staged model swap with traffic drain.
- Kernel scheduler misclassification: rare cases where multitenant co-location causes credit starvation. Mitigation: enable quota isolation for top 3 high-priority routes.
- Fidelity probe sampling bias: small corpora can underrepresent failure modes. Mitigation: expand corpus with adversarial prompts and stratified sampling across customers.

Operational metrics to publish weekly
----------------------------------
- % routes meeting p95 target
- Median fidelity delta across active experiments
- Number of automatic rollbacks initiated by LFG
- Cost per 1M tokens for routes using adaptive batching

Ownership and contacts

- PagerDuty: runtime-oncall team (primary).

Appendix: example LFG config snippet
----------------------------------
(Place under /etc/runtime-governor/policies/latency-fidelity.yml)

```yaml
policy_name: latency_fidelity_default
routes:
  - name: /v1/generate-short
    slo_p95_ms: 120
    fidelity_budget: 0.005   # allowed relative delta
    admission_share: 0.9
    kernel_preferences:
      - stable_prec
      - fast_fwd
  - name: /v1/completions-long
    slo_p95_ms: 600
    fidelity_budget: 0.02
    admission_share: 0.7
    kernel_preferences:
      - fast_fwd
```

Appendix: minimal experiment commands
------------------------------------
- Start an experiment: 
  runtimectl experiment start --name latfidelity-july --policy /etc/runtime-governor/policies/latency-fidelity.yml --traffic-split 0.01 --shadow true
- Collect traces for 1h: 
  runtimectl collect --exp latfidelity-july --duration 1h --out /tmp/latfidelity-trace.tar
